A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PBR-NeRF and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite revised experiments and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original PBR-NeRF experiments on NeILF++ and DTU, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative reconstructions, and loss ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments, revised benchmark results, geometry measurements, and expanded loss ablations.

M1.justification: The BRDF, incident-light, and NeRF/SDF fields, two proposed physics-based losses, and three optimization phases remain unchanged. The expanded diagram and explanation of the SDF's two uses clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six NeILF++ illumination conditions and 15 DTU scans for reconstruction and novel view synthesis. The added geometry measurements assess an existing model output on retained data; the broader ablation uses conditions already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes Neural-PIL from the DTU RGB comparison and introduces VolSDF and NeuS for geometry comparison. Table 1 retains PhySG, SG-ENV, NeILF, and NeILF++ as comparators.

E3.justification: V2 extends SSIM reporting to the main NeILF++ comparison and adds DTU Chamfer Distance evaluation against reference point clouds. Table 3 changes from City-only scores to averages over all six illumination conditions. Appendix A also changes the ablation sampling from 128 incident directions to the full method's 256.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands the three-variant ablation into all four combinations of the two losses, adding the previously missing specular-loss-only test and evaluating their contributions across six conditions. Appendix A and Figure 6 provide corresponding qualitative evidence. The DTU case studies add normal comparisons and replace scan 40 with scan 105.

E5.justification: Table 2 adds standard deviations to the DTU summary scores for PBR-NeRF and NeILF++. Both versions already report averaging three training runs, so this establishes additional uncertainty reporting rather than an increase in run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 contain substantial replacements and additions. Reported PBR-NeRF mean albedo PSNR changes from 19.09 to 20.08 in Table 1, and DTU RGB PSNR from 28.22 to 28.63 in Table 2. Baseline scores also change, SSIM and Chamfer results are added, and qualitative outputs are updated. The ablation results use different aggregation and sampling, and the PDFs do not establish a controlled version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and appendix derivations are retained. Equation (9) gains the reflection-loss weight already specified in v1 Equation (21) and Table 5, harmonizing existing mathematics. New Appendix C supplies qualitative intuition about energy violations rather than a new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two physics-based priors for joint inverse rendering, improved material estimation, and competitive novel view synthesis. The expanded evaluation supports these retained claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains SG-Env's advantage under environment lighting and weakness under mixed lighting, acknowledges inferior metallicness SSIM, and explains why clipping and unknown tone mapping prevent reliable DTU lighting estimation. New Appendix C discusses mechanisms of BRDF energy creation and loss. Existing reflective-surface and fine-detail limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies an 8192-ray batch and 5K/1K/30K iterations for the geometry/material/joint phases, replacing v1's less specific 30K-iteration description. Reported hardware and runtime change from an RTX 4090 and 1–3 hours to an A6000 and 3–7.5 hours. Appendix D.2 additionally explains the two SDF uses during joint training; the code link and loss-weight tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a substantive comparison between SG-Env's explicit lighting representation and PBR-NeRF's more flexible implicit representation. The same 55 works remain cited, and the principal related-work positioning is retained; bibliographic metadata changes do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the related-work, method, and experimental discussions, plus terminology and affiliation edits. A short new Appendix C shifts the existing background appendix to D. The main section sequence and most explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are rearranged or redrawn, Table 1 gains PSNR/SSIM subcolumns, and Table 2 adds geometry rows and uncertainty reporting while moving earlier. Figure 5 adds reference columns and a normals row; Figure 6 gains an ablation column. Figure 7 is relocated and its qualitative outputs are updated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contributions: the complete six-condition ablation isolates both losses, and quantitative geometry comparisons directly test a reconstruction capability previously lacking numerical evaluation. Added uncertainty reporting, SSIM comparisons, and training details improve transparency. A small inconsistency remains—Appendix A claims an energy-only metallicness PSNR improvement although Table 3 shows 21.35 decreasing to 21.30—but it does not outweigh the stronger empirical support.
